questions.question: Differential erosion means:
options: Soft layers are stripped quickly while hard layers survive and stand proud
All rock layers erode at exactly the same rate
Rivers erode but wind does not

questions.question: The resistant horizontal sheets in the Karoo are made of:
options: DOLERITE — molten rock that squeezed between the layers about 180 million years ago and cooled into tough sills

questions.question: A cap rock protects a hill by:
options: Shielding the soft layers beneath it like a hard hat, so the hill keeps a flat top and steep sides
Attracting lightning away from the slopes

questions.question: The basaltic plateau of Lesotho and the high Drakensberg was built by:
options: Stacked basalt LAVA flows that behave exactly like horizontal strata

subtopics.title: From Plateau to Pointed Koppie — the Landform Family

questions.question: A mesa differs from a butte in that a mesa is:
options: WIDER than it is high, with a broad flat cap — a butte is higher than it is wide with a small summit

questions.question: The Three Sisters near Beaufort West are:
options: Dolerite-capped BUTTES standing in file on the Karoo plain

questions.question: A conical hill or pointed koppie forms when:
options: A river deposits a cone of sediment
The protective cap is finally breached and stripped, letting the soft layers beneath weather into a cone
Wind piles sand around a bush

questions.question: The correct erosional sequence for horizontal strata is:
options: Butte, mesa, plateau, plain, conical hill
Conical hill, butte, mesa, plateau, plain
Plain, conical hill, plateau, mesa, butte
Plateau, mesa, butte, conical hill, plain

questions.question: In scarp retreat, the eroding cliff:
options: Keeps roughly the same steep angle but ends up positioned further BACK — the slope retreats parallel to itself
Becomes gentler and rounder with time
Grows steadily steeper until it overhangs

questions.question: Back wasting differs from down wasting because back wasting:
options: Lowers the summit from the top
Wears slopes back SIDEWAYS while they keep their shape, instead of flattening the surface from above

questions.question: The gently sloping rock floor left at the foot of a retreating scarp is a:
A pediplain is formed when:
options: Pediments from scarps retreating on opposite sides meet and merge into a wide, nearly level erosion plain dotted with surviving koppies

subtopics.title: Canyons and the Mapwork of Flat Country

questions.question: A canyon in horizontal strata has step-like walls because:
options: Hard bands stand out as vertical cliffs while soft bands weather back into slopes
Earthquakes shake the walls loose evenly
All the layers are equally strong

questions.question: On a contour map, a mesa appears as:
options: Widely spaced contours with no pattern
Closed contours with a WIDE empty summit ringed by tightly crowded contours marking the cliff

questions.question: With a vertical scale of 1 cm to 20 m and a horizontal scale of 1:50 000, the vertical exaggeration is:
options: 25 times — vertical scale 1:2 000, so 50 000 divided by 2 000

questions.question: A climb of 200 m over a horizontal distance of 1 000 m is a gradient of:
options: 1 in 5 — height difference over distance in the same units, 200 over 1 000

questions.question: In the cake picture, the rock-hard icing stands for:
options: The dolerite cap that protects the soft shale sponge beneath it

questions.question: The children picking at the cake always eat the sponge first because:
options: Soft layers weather and erode faster than hard ones — differential erosion

questions.question: A dead-flat Karoo skyline tells you:
options: There was never any erosion there
A hard cap layer is still unbroken and on duty up top

questions.question: In the shape code, table, stool and traffic cone stand for:
The hill turns from stool to traffic cone at the moment when:
options: The dolerite hard hat is finally picked through, leaving the soft rock unprotected to round into a cone

questions.question: The five-age countdown of the landscape reads:
options: Table-land, table, stool, cone, flat — plateau, mesa, butte, conical hill, plain

questions.question: The Karoo is world-famous to geographers because:
options: It has the world's highest mountains
It is the only place with rivers
All five generations of the landform family can often be seen standing in a single view

questions.question: The retreating-soldier picture means Karoo cliffs:
options: Keep their steep face to the end, simply rebuilding it a little further back each time — parallel retreat
Slowly slump into round soft hills
Stay in exactly the same place forever

questions.question: The winter mechanism that levers blocks off the cliff face is:
options: Water freezing in cracks, swelling and wedging the blocks loose

questions.question: The cleared floor a retreating army leaves behind stands for:
options: The PEDIMENT — the smooth rock apron left at the foot of a retreating scarp, which merges with others into a pediplain

questions.question: When a large river attacks horizontal strata it produces:
options: A CANYON cut straight down, with stepped walls — like the Fish River Canyon and the Blyde River Canyon
